title: FOMC communications blackout begins (through 2027-12-09) — the last of the eight 2027 windows, covering the year's final meeting and final SEP
source: EST: THE WINDOW IS THIS REPO'S OWN DECODE, CITED RATHER THAN RE-RUN. federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/fomc-blackout-period-calendar.pdf had its content streams inflated and its shaded cells decoded in-session on 2026-09-05 by the fomc-blackout-start-2027-04-17 research already in this calendar -- a decode THIS session did not re-run and does not claim to have re-run. That entry's source field records the decoded 2027 windows verbatim: "Jan 16-28, Mar 6-18, Apr 17-29, May 29 -> Jun 10, Jul 17-29, Sep 4-16, Oct 16-28, NOV 27 -> DEC 9", validated there against the PDF's 2026 page (which returned Sep 5-17 / Oct 17-29 / Nov 28 -> Dec 10, matching three sibling ledgers exactly). CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY HERE BY THE BOARD'S OWN STATED RULE, re-derived rather than assumed, against a meeting date this session re-fetched: the policy footnote reads verbatim "the blackout period will begin at 12:00 a.m. Eastern Time the second Saturday before a meeting ... if the Committee meeting starts on a Tuesday, the blackout period will begin at the start of the Saturday that falls ten days earlier". federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this session (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, page stamp "Last Update: August 19, 2026"), gives the 2027 panel verbatim as "January 26-27 | March 16-17* | April 27-28 | June 8-9* | July 27-28 | September 14-15* | October 26-27 | December 7-8*". Dec 7 2027 is a TUESDAY (computed, not assumed), ten days earlier is SATURDAY 2027-11-27, and the meeting ends Wednesday Dec 8 so the window closes at the end of Thursday 2027-12-09 -- the decoded shading and the stated rule return the same two dates independently. The same arithmetic reproduces all seven 2027 blackout entries this calendar already carries (01-16, 03-06, 04-17, 05-29, 07-17, 09-04, 10-16) to the day. Filed estimate because it is a firm rule and a decoded shading applied to a TENTATIVE meeting date -- fomccalendars.htm states verbatim "Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it", so the promotion trigger is the 2027-10-26/27 meeting ratifying December 7-8, not a better fetch. Discovered during the fomc-2027-10-27 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the fomc-2027-10-27 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). THE GAP IS EXACT AND MECHANICAL: of the eight 2027 FOMC blackout windows this repo decoded, SEVEN are tracked as fomc-blackout-start-<date> entries (2027-01-16, 03-06, 04-17, 05-29, 07-17, 09-04, 10-16) and this is the only one absent. It surfaced from this lane's own corridor rather than from a scan: the October 26-27 meeting is the CONFIRMING VENUE for December 7-8 under the Board's tentative-dates rule, so reading forward from it is what exposed the missing window. IMPACT medium matches the family -- every fomc-blackout-start-* entry in this calendar is medium, and this lane does not re-litigate a sibling class's tier from outside it. THREE NOTES FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT. (1) THIS IS THE YEAR'S LAST WINDOW AND IT COVERS THE FINAL SEP. December 7-8 carries the asterisk on the Board's own panel, so unlike the October meeting this one publishes projections -- the blackout therefore runs into the year's most information-dense Fed event, not its quietest. (2) IT INHERITS A CHAIN OF TENTATIVE DATES, and the chain is worth stating: this window's date depends on the December meeting's date, which is tentative until the October 26-27 meeting confirms it, which is itself tentative until the September 14-15 meeting confirms THAT. Three links, all estimate, and the ledger's caution should widen accordingly rather than treating the arithmetic's cleanliness as confirmation. (3) NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED HERE. symbols is empty, no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed, and this lane's own measurements were about calendar integrity, not about blackout windows -- its conclusions do not transfer. THIS IS A COMPETING PROPOSAL, DELIBERATELY, AND THE COMPETITION IS THE POINT. The window was untracked at the tip this lane branched from (04aec2c8); commit a5990340 (PR #1966, the consumer-confidence-2027-11-30 lane) merged mid-session carrying proposals/fomc-blackout-start-2027-11-27.from-consumer-confidence-2027-11-30.json -- the same two dates, discovered the same day from a different starting event. This file is filed rather than withdrawn because #1717's naming scheme is built for exactly this (--validate warns on competing proposals; the first by file name stands in until a canonical exists, and this one sorts second, so it changes nothing the calendar serves), and because the two derivations are INDEPENDENT: the sibling reached the window from the December print corridor, this lane reached it from the October meeting's confirming-venue chain and re-derived the ten-days-earlier rule against a fomccalendars.htm fetch of its own. An estimate resting on a decoded PDF shading is exactly the kind of claim that wants a second, differently-routed derivation, and now has one. Whichever lane writes the canonical fomc-blackout-start-2027-11-27.json should read both files and may then prune both. Proposed as an estimate; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
